Name Recognition listing copy vs name-detection engineering — two different jobs

Teams assume called-name alert capability covers storefront language. iOS, Speech APIs, and Connect actually separate in-app name listening from product-page copy:

  • Name Recognition in the app — on-device listening for the user's name or nicknames, notification routing when a name is detected, integration with system Name Recognition settings, and microphone permission flows. Engineering inside the binary — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Speech and audio pipeline implementation — distinguishing name detection from ambient sound classifiers, ensuring alerts fire reliably in headphones-on scenarios, and testing notification UX when someone nearby says the user's name. Engineering — not listing rewrite.
  • Called-name marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app supports Name Recognition or called-name alerts. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Name Recognition support in the app.

A Name Recognition-compatible app and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe called-name notification value on the store page, not whether name detection runs inside the app.

Name Recognition vs Sound Recognition, Speak Screen, Live Speech, Live Listen, and Voice Control — disambiguation

Apple groups several hearing and speech features under Accessibility. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers Name Recognition and called-name alert marketing on listing metadata — not the other toggles:

  • Name Recognition (this page) — iOS listens for the user's name or nicknames spoken nearby and sends a notification. Useful with headphones on or for hearing accessibility. Gallery frames may show Settings → Sound & Name Recognition → Name Recognition toggles, called-name notification previews, or "Notify when someone says my name" badges. zh-Hans terms: 姓名识别, 名字识别, 叫到名字时通知. Apple documents English-name listening; listing copy must stay honest to that scope.
  • Sound Recognition (different) — alerts for alarms, doorbells, animals, smoke alarms, and other environmental sounds — 声音识别. Same parent pane (Sound & Name Recognition / 声音与姓名识别) but a different listener. See Sound Recognition listing guide — environmental sound alerts are not called-name notifications.
  • Spoken Content / Speak Screen (different) — the device reads on-screen text aloud — 说出内容 / 朗读屏幕. See Speak Screen listing guide — text-to-speech reading is not listening for your name.
  • Live Speech / Personal Voice (different) — the user types or speaks as their own synthesized voice for FaceTime and communication — not listening for names nearby. See Live Speech listing guide and Personal Voice listing guide — outbound voice output is not inbound name detection.
  • Live Listen / Hearing Devices (different) — microphone streaming to AirPods or Made for iPhone hearing aids for conversation amplification — 实时收听 / 助听设备. See Live Listen listing guide and Hearing Devices listing guide — hearing-aid streaming is not name-called alert marketing.
  • Voice Control / Vocal Shortcuts (different) — speech commands to control the device or trigger custom spoken phrases — not passive name detection notifications. See Voice Control listing guide and Vocal Shortcuts listing guide — command-and-control speech is not notify-when-someone-says-my-name listening.
  • Headphone Accommodations / Background Sounds (different) — headphone EQ tuning and ambient focus loops under Hearing — not name recognition. See Headphone Accommodations listing guide and Background Sounds listing guide when those are your lead claims.
  • VoiceOver (different) — screen reader navigation — not called-name alerts. See VoiceOver listing guide.

Your gallery may show a Name Recognition toggle on one frame and a Sound Recognition sound-type picker on the next — but listing copy should name each claim accurately per frame. A called-name notification demo is not a baby-cry alert, not a Speak Screen read-aloud panel, not a Live Listen AirPods walkthrough, and not a Voice Control command sheet unless that is what the screenshot shows.

What Name Recognition actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships Name Recognition in iOS and iPadOS Settings → Accessibility → Sound & Name Recognition. When enabled, the device listens for the user's name or nicknames spoken nearby and sends a notification — helpful when wearing headphones or for hearing accessibility. Apple notes that Name Recognition listens for English names and is not intended for emergency reliance. Third-party apps may complement this with called-name alert workflows your binary actually ships. AppLocale rewrites listing copy from what your US page already claims:

  • If your app complements system Name Recognition — zh-Hans copy can describe called-name notifications, nickname support, or headphones-on name alerts your binary actually ships — without claiming to replace the system setting or detect every language unless your English listing already states that accurately.
  • If your app ships custom called-name alert UX — description and screenshot overlays should name the notification benefits you deliver (姓名识别, 叫到名字时通知, 有人叫名字时提醒) in commerce-idiomatic Chinese, not generic "always hears your name" overclaims.
  • Separate Name Recognition from Sound Recognition in copy — Sound Recognition alerts for environmental sounds like doorbells and smoke alarms; Name Recognition alerts when someone says your name. Listing vocabulary must follow your English lead feature and gallery frames.
  • No medical or emergency claims — do not imply Name Recognition replaces hearing aids, medical monitoring, or emergency alerting in zh-Hans copy unless your English listing already makes that claim — and AppLocale does not certify safety outcomes.
  • If your US page overclaims — AppLocale aligns zh-Hans strings to your English source; we do not invent broader Name Recognition scope than your screenshots and description support.

Clear zh-Hans copy helps buyers who rely on called-name notifications understand your feature story before install. It does not replace Speech framework implementation, microphone permissions, or Apple's review decisions — and it does not promise the device will always hear every name in every environment.

Name Recognition-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Called-name marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Name Recognition — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Name Recognition vs generic "name alerts"

US pages use "Notify when someone says my name", "Name Recognition support", or "Called-name alerts." China storefront copy often uses 姓名识别, 叫到名字时通知, or 有人叫名字时提醒 — depending on whether you mean Apple's Name Recognition setting specifically, custom in-app called-name workflows, or general notification UX. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope, not inventing Name Recognition support your app does not ship.

Name Recognition vs Sound Recognition — same pane, different feature

Both settings live under Sound & Name Recognition (声音与姓名识别). Name Recognition listens for the user's name — 姓名识别. Sound Recognition listens for environmental sounds like doorbells and smoke alarms — 声音识别. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 声音识别 when your English source only markets called-name notifications. See the Sound Recognition listing guide only if ambient sound alerts are your lead marketing claim.

Name Recognition vs Speak Screen and Live Speech

Speak Screen reads on-screen text aloud — 朗读屏幕. Live Speech lets the user type and speak as their own voice — outbound communication, not inbound name listening. Name Recognition passively listens for names spoken nearby — 叫到名字时通知. Each surface has distinct buyer vocabulary and should not appear interchangeably in one keyword field unless your English listing genuinely markets all three.

Name Recognition vs Live Listen and Hearing Devices

Live Listen streams live microphone audio to AirPods for conversation amplification — 实时收听. Hearing Devices covers MFi hearing-aid pairing and audiology hardware — 助听设备. Name Recognition sends a notification when someone says your name — different buyer intent from streaming or hardware pairing. zh-Hans copy should not imply 实时收听 when your gallery only shows called-name notification demos.

English-name listening scope

Apple documents that Name Recognition listens for English names. zh-Hans listing copy can describe the called-name notification benefit honestly — 有人叫名字时提醒 — without over-specifying language coverage or claiming detection in every acoustic environment unless your English gallery shows that consistently.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need called-name search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 姓名识别, 叫到名字时通知, and 名字识别 each signal different intent from 声音识别 Sound Recognition keywords.

Caption lines vs burned-in badges

Marketing screenshot overlays you control — "Notify when someone says my name" headlines on gallery frames showing Settings → Accessibility → Sound & Name Recognition → Name Recognition — are separate caption fields or burned-in PNG text. See Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese for caption-field mechanics when overlays are editable in Connect.

What is Apple Name Recognition and why does listing copy matter?

Name Recognition is under Settings → Accessibility → Sound & Name Recognition → Name Recognition.
